routeSelection.basis: The generic target offers eight formally named areas and their associated languages without identifying one as the general or representative route. Africa is the first area in the official order and Arabic is the first language listed for that area, so this complete pathway is selected neutrally and without regard to UCR fit. First-listed choices are likewise used where the curriculum requires one research-methods or thematic-seminar option.

comparator.sourceNotes: The current official programme page confirms that students choose one of eight world regions and an associated language, combine cultural, historical, political and economic approaches, and complete research methods, a thematic seminar, 30 EC of elective space, the PRINS consultancy project and an area-specific thesis. The latest complete official study guide supplies a coherent 180-EC structure: 60 EC in each year. Africa and Arabic are selected by the neutral official-order tie-break for the generic target. Genuine elective space remains open, and no host courses or minor are invented.

exception.reason: Leiden International Studies is not merely a broad collection of global politics, economics, history and culture courses. Every student selects one world region, studies that region through all four disciplinary perspectives, completes a cumulative 25-EC associated-language sequence plus a 5-EC language-and-culture-in-practice course, and writes an area-specific thesis. UCR offers strong adjacent work in international relations, economics, history, law, sociology, media and sustainability, but its current curriculum contains only one general Dutch course and no sustained regional-language sequence. It also lacks a coherent four-perspective area curriculum for any one of the eight Leiden regions. Filling 24 UCR slots with globally oriented courses would therefore reproduce breadth while discarding the degree's defining language-plus-regional-specialisation architecture.
exception.curriculumContext: The latest complete official study-guide table accounts for exactly 180 EC: 60 EC per year. Year 1 establishes academic literacy, cultural studies, economics, politics, sociolinguistics and world history, then begins a selected region through culture/language, history and 10 EC of language acquisition. Year 2 adds the region's economy and politics, cross-cultural communication, research methods, global political economy, international relations, philosophy of science, a thematic seminar and 15 further EC in the same language. Year 3 contains 30 EC of genuine elective space and requires a 10-EC consultancy project, 5 EC of language and culture in practice, and a 15-EC area-specific thesis. Africa with Arabic is instantiated only by the official-order tie-break; the same structural mismatch applies to all eight areas and their linked languages.
exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 records in the current GitHub main data/reference/ucr_courses_enriched.xlsx (SHA-256 7bf6c2ae9de0837086ec741c27bd94ed7e85dff2d25bde619ecd50cc4d685879), including names, descriptions, outline-derived profiles, disciplines, topics, methods, prerequisites and planned availability. BENECON111 Introduction to Economics, BENECON211 International Macroeconomics, GOSPOLI212 Theory of International Relations, GOSPOLI313 Peace & Conflict, GOSHIST111 Modern History, GOSHIST211 History of Empires, GOSLAWJ111 Human Rights: Law & Philosophy, GOSLAWJ212 Introduction to Public International Law, GOSSOCI212 Qualitative Research Methodology and ENSDELT312 Governance of Sustainability cover much of the global economics, politics, history, justice, methods and sustainability breadth. MCCHEAM211 African Art & Heritage and MCCMEDI311 Media & Race provide valuable regionally relevant cultural perspectives, while BENENTR312 International Business & Governance and the communication curriculum support international professional applications. However, the workbook has no Arabic course and no cumulative foreign-language pathway; MCCCOMM112 Dutch is the only named language-acquisition course. It also has no four-course Africa sequence spanning culture/language, history, economy and politics, and no language-in-practice course or area-specific thesis seminar. Other Leiden routes face the same absence of a linked 30-EC language progression and coherent regional spine. These omissions affect the organizing structure of all three years and cannot be repaired through the 30-EC elective space.
